safeguards.missing_stale_disputed: Block usable calculation; unknown is never zero.
safeguards.si_evidence: 4Ps status and document count do not assign SI points; do not duplicate HI as SI.
safeguards.pool_change: Freeze the new complete pool, recalculate its bounds and every affected result, and preserve the prior run.

safeguards.selection: Scores and ranks do not automatically select beneficiaries or record actual assistance.
safeguards.history: Preserve exact policy, weight, source, input, bounds, calculation and human-decision history.

si_rubric.title: Reviewed barriers to essential needs
si_rubric.description: A trained, authorized assessor assigns one level after a documented assessment. This is a new proposal, not a rubric supplied by the DOCX.
domains: Access to necessary care and daily support

levels.description: Accepted assessment confirms no unmet barrier in the listed domains during the assessment period.
Occasional shortfall in at least one domain, without a recurrent or current critical barrier.
A recurrent unmet barrier in one domain, without a current critical barrier or recurrent barriers in two domains.
A current critical unmet barrier in any domain, or recurrent unmet barriers in at least two domains.

si_rubric.application: Consider levels 4, 3, 2, then 1; choose the highest supported level. Missing or disputed assessment receives no level. Review must define occasional, recurrent and critical before adoption.
si_rubric.overlap_control: Do not add points for income amount, employment category, household count, past releases, disability label, 4Ps membership, or number of documents. Assess the documented barriers themselves.
si_rubric.review_needed: Association authority must approve or replace this rubric, assessor qualifications, evidence standards, operational definitions, correction process and consistency checks.

assessment_periods.HI: Monthly average over the three complete calendar months before the program application closing date; income composition remains unresolved.
assessment_periods.SI: Assess the same three-month period and current barriers at a common documented evaluation cutoff.
assessment_periods.ES: Accepted employment category at the common evaluation cutoff; mixed, changing and unlisted categories remain unresolved.
assessment_periods.HM: Accepted household composition at the common evaluation cutoff.
assessment_periods.cutoff: Use one timezone-aware program evaluation cutoff; freeze it with the pool. Review evidence freshness and changes after closing before adoption.

household_definition.description: Include the applicant and people who usually share the same dwelling and food or essential-expense budget. This is a household count, not a dependent count.
household_definition.review_needed: Define usual residence, temporary absence, shared housing with separate budgets, split households, caregivers, boarders and institutional living.

pa_scope.description: Count confirmed, non-voided actual assistance releases across Association programs during the 12 calendar months ending at the common evaluation cutoff.
pa_scope.interval: Proposed interval: cutoff shifted back 12 calendar months, inclusive, through cutoff, inclusive; leap-day/month-end behavior needs a recorded rule.
pa_scope.review_needed: Decide release-unit/deduplication rules, external assistance, legacy imports and incomplete history. No retained rows alone cannot establish a complete zero-release history.

ranking_convention.description: Descending exact score, competition ranks 1, 2, 2, 4. Equal exact scores share a rank and tie group. Display rounding never decides a tie.
ranking_convention.boundary_ties: Hold the unresolved capacity-boundary tie for an authorized human procedure. No hidden winner from name, submission time, database ID or row order.
ranking_convention.selection: Retain a separate human selection record within authorized slots; ranking does not publish recipients or record release.

unresolved_decisions.question: Authorize or revise the documented ES mapping, dataset method, disclosed directions and weighted sum for this new operational version.
Who may adopt the proposed SI assessment, and which rubric, assessor qualifications, definitions, calibration and correction procedure are authorized?
What happens when maximum equals minimum, including a single eligible applicant? No zero, maximum, midpoint or weight redistribution is adopted.

Specify gross/net basis; wages, self-employment, irregular work, pensions, remittances, benefits, one-off transfers, in-kind income and exclusions; prevent duplicates and define zero/negative adjustments.
Define self-employed, informal, retired, student, unpaid caregiver, unable-to-work, multiple-job and changing categories without silently mapping them to unemployed.

Authorize evidence types and accessible alternatives, acceptance/rejection/dispute handling, freshness, reviewer authority, unavailable evidence and re-review. Raw registration fields are not accepted inputs.
Define evidence of complete PA coverage, missing legacy/external history and a justified zero. Determine treatment of unverified prior assistance without imputing zero.
Adopt or replace the proposed three-month assessment periods and common cutoff, including income averaging, evidence freshness, date boundaries and post-closing changes.
Adopt a household definition and decide ambiguous living arrangements, temporary absence and membership changes.
Adopt scope/window and define qualifying release units, installments, duplicates, external/imported records and month-end date handling.
Adopt competition ranking and authorize the human procedure and audit requirements for capacity-boundary ties.
Define evaluation closure and the complete eligible inventory, unresolved cases, late corrections, full-pool recalculation and treatment of already selected/published cases.

Identify a separately authorized immutable weighting method/version applicable to this new engine. Existing source/weight-only approvals and illustrative ratio matrices do not authorize this method. No weights are reapproved here.
Review exact-rational comparisons and half-even two-decimal display. Decide whether classification is omitted or separately authorized; document example bands are not activated.
Identify institutional approver, program scope, effective dates, audit evidence and explicit adoption/migration rules. No approved record is created by this draft.

readiness_contract.policy: Complete and authorize definitions, encodings, methods, source/evidence rules, edge cases, ranking, weight reference, authority and scope. Numerical dataset bounds are not required at this stage.
readiness_contract.applicant_data: At evaluation, freeze the complete accepted eligible inventory, cutoff, accepted evidence identities/versions and verified history coverage; then compute the shared numerical bounds. Missing, stale, disputed or unresolved inputs stop a usable run.
readiness_contract.operational: Both readiness checks, a valid immutable approved policy binding, accepted-evidence integration and explicit operational enablement are required. This draft satisfies none of the authorization requirements.

versioning_contract.draft_revision: Append a new revision with predecessor digest; never edit or overwrite a retained revision.
versioning_contract.approval: A separate authorized service must record a complete immutable policy version and its audit/effective scope. There is no approval or activation operation in this draft implementation.
versioning_contract.program_binding: A program using the new engine must reference the exact approved policy ID, revision and content digest plus its authorized weight-version reference. A mutable latest-draft pointer is forbidden.
versioning_contract.rebind: Draft edits and newer shared versions cannot rebind programs. Any later authorized rebind is explicit, audited and versioned; preserve prior links and runs and apply the approved correction rules.
versioning_contract.run_snapshot: Retain the bound policy and weight snapshots/digests, complete pool/evidence versions, cutoff, computed bounds, directions, exact traces and separate human decisions. Replay from these snapshots, never from the current shared draft.
